discussion.author: ef74e4b
discussion.html:
A. Review the development network routing table.
The site-to-site VPN tunnel is established, so the tunnel and ciphers are working. Client VPN users can connect successfully, meaning ACLs/security rules are likely correct.
A missing or incorrect route in the development network routing table would allow traffic in, but prevent traffic back out to the office

discussion.author: ef74e4b
discussion.html:
A. Review the development network routing table.

The VPN tunnel is up, so not a cipher or restart issue. If ACLs were the issue, the client VPN users would fail too.

discussion.html: Traffic is reaching the development network: Confirmed by firewall flow logs.

discussion.author: Niels123
discussion.html: I should first check the routing table!

discussion.html:

⸻

Explanation:

The key clues are:
	•	The VPN tunnel is established and traffic is reaching the development network from the office (confirmed by flow logs).
	•	Developers outside the office (on client VPN) can connect to development resources.
	•	Developers inside the office cannot, even though traffic is reaching the destination.
	•	The office and client VPN have different IP subnets.

This points to a routing issue on the development network side. The development network may have routes defined only for the client VPN subnet, but not for the office subnet, meaning replies to the office traffic don’t get routed back properly.

discussion.author: 6f7e8ce

This suggests the issue is not with the tunnel itself, but rather with routing:
The development network likely doesn’t have a proper route back to the office subnet. If there's no return route, the initial request reaches the cloud, but the response has nowhere to go — effectively breaking communication.

question_html: A DevOps engineer is performing maintenance on the mail servers for a company’s web application. Part of this maintenance includes checking core operating system updates. The servers are currently running version 3.2 of the operating system. The engineer has two update options—one to version 4.1 and the other to version 3.7. discussion.author: fc040c7
discussion.html:
Major vs. Minor Upgrades: Moving from version 3.2 to 4.1 is a major version upgrade. These typically include architectural changes, deprecated features, or breaking API changes that could crash the mail server or web application.
Due Diligence: Before touching any environment (Dev or Prod), an engineer must understand the compatibility requirements. Release notes will specify if version 4.1 requires a different database version, more RAM, or specific configuration changes that version 3.7 (a minor update) might not.

discussion.author: ef74e4b
discussion.html:
C. Read the release notes on version 4.1

When faced with multiple supported versions, especially a major version upgrade, always:
Review release notes first before testing or deploying.

discussion.author: veteran_tech
discussion.html: Considering these are mail servers supporting a web application, I would test on a DevNet to see if anything breaks.  Just my two cents, no harm in reading the release notes, I see this through the prism of change management and risk.  High impact if the mail servers go down in production (seen a guy get fired for not having a reliable Exchange backup server) again my Mr. Spock logic says A.

discussion.author: Justheretolook
discussion.html:
The correct answer is:

✅ C. Read the release notes on version 4.1

⸻

Explanation:

Before performing any OS upgrade, especially from major version 3.x to 4.x, it’s essential to:
	•	Understand the changes introduced in the newer version
	•	Identify any breaking changes, deprecated features, or incompatibilities

question_text: A DevOps engineer is receiving reports that users can no longer access the company’s web application after hardening of a web server. discussion.author: ef74e4b
discussion.html:

discussion.author: Justheretolook
discussion.html:
The correct answer is:

✅ B. Configure TLS 1.2 or newer.

⸻

ERR_SSL_VERSION_OR_CIPHER_MISMATCH

Occurs when the client browser and the server cannot agree on a common SSL/TLS version or cipher suite. This often happens when:
	•	The server has been hardened and older SSL/TLS versions or insecure ciphers have been disabled
	•	The client is using an outdated browser or device that doesn’t support modern protocols

The most reliable fix is to:
	•	Ensure the web server is configured to support TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3, which are:
	•	Secure
	•	Widely supported by modern browsers
	•	Recommended by security standards (e.g., PCI DSS)

question_text: A cloud deployment uses three different VPCs. The subnets on each VPC need to communicate with the others over private channels. Which of the following will achieve this objective?
question_html: A cloud deployment uses three different VPCs. The subnets on each VPC need to communicate with the others over private channels. Which of the following will achieve this objective?

options.A: Deploying a load balancer to send traffic to the private IP addresses
options.B: Creating peering connections between all VPCs
options.C: Adding BGP routes using the VPCs’ private IP addresses
options.D: Establishing identical routing tables on all VPCs

discussion.author: ef74e4b
discussion.html:
B. Creating peering connections between all VPCs

To allow private communication between multiple VPCs, use VPC peering between each VPC.
-Load balancers are for distributing traffic to resources, not connecting entire VPCs.
-BGP is used in VPNs or Direct Connect, not simple VPC-to-VPC communication.
-Routing tables alone don’t create connectivity; peering or VPNs are required.

discussion.author: Justheretolook
discussion.html:
The correct answer is:

✅ B. Creating peering connections between all VPCs

⸻

Explanation:

To allow private communication between subnets in different VPCs, you need to establish VPC peering connections.
	•	VPC Peering enables direct, private communication between VPCs using private IPs, without needing to route over the public internet.
	•	Once peering is set up, you’ll also need to update route tables in each VPC to allow traffic to flow between them.

In this scenario (3 VPCs), you’d need full mesh peering:
	•	VPC A ↔ VPC B
	•	VPC A ↔ VPC C
	•	VPC B ↔ VPC C

This allows all VPCs to communicate directly and privately with each other.

discussion.author: ef74e4b
discussion.html:
D. Ansible

CI/CD pipelines automate the deployment of VMs (or other resources) to an IaaS environment. Once a VM is running, you want to harden the operating system—this means applying security configurations, patching, and enforcing policies. Ansible is a configuration management and automation tool. You can write playbooks that automatically configure and harden the OS, install updates, disable unnecessary services, and enforce security baselines.

The others don’t fit this purpose:

A. Docker - Container runtime, not for hardening VMs.

B. Kubernetes - Orchestration platform for containers, not OS-level hardening.

C. Git - Version control, used for code management, not system hardening.

discussion.author: Justheretolook
discussion.html:
The correct answer is:

✅ D. Ansible

⸻

Explanation:

Ansible is a configuration management and automation tool that can be used to harden operating systems by:
	•	Disabling unused services
	•	Enforcing strong password policies
	•	Applying security patches
	•	Configuring firewalls
	•	Managing user access and permissions

Once a VM is deployed via a CI/CD pipeline in an IaaS environment, Ansible can be run to apply these hardening rules in an automated and repeatable way.

For compliance purposes, when data needs to be retained for 10 years or more with minimal access, the most cost-efficient cloud storage tier is Archive. Other tiers like Hot, Warm, and Cold are more expensive and intended for frequently or semi-frequently accessed data. While retrieval from Archive may take longer, this delay is generally acceptable for compliance-related storage.

discussion.html: Blue Green avoids risk by having two online environments for full testing.  Canary limits risk by deploying to a small group.  If the expectation is to completely avoid loss, then Blue-Green makes more sense to be.

discussion.author: ef74e4b
discussion.html:
B. Blue-green

To deploy a new web application version to many servers without causing outages, implement a blue-green deployment. This strategy uses two identical environments, switches traffic to the new version only after verification, and allows instant rollback if issues occur. Rolling, canary, or round-robin strategies do not fully prevent downtime.

discussion.author: Justheretolook
discussion.html:
The correct answer is:

✅ C. Canary

⸻

Explanation:

Canary deployments involve releasing the new version to a small subset of servers/users first, while the rest continue to use the old version. This approach allows engineers to monitor for issues in a controlled way, and rollback quickly if something goes wrong — reducing the risk of outages.

A company’s cybersecurity team receives the following alert that a production VM was deleted from the virtual network:

21 September 09:19:08 (GMT-5)
Resource with ID: PROD-WEB001 was deleted by User: Logging

Service -

The console to manage virtual network resources uses directory authentication. Only users in a particular directory group can interactively access the virtual network management console. The logging service account is not part of this group and requires some local administration privileges to aggregate logs from various resources. The cybersecurity team discovers that the logging service account was previously given full directory administration privileges and they see the following entry:

21 September 09:10:55 (GMT-5)
User with ID: Logging Service was added to the Group: VNet
Console Administrators by actor: Logging Service.

The cybersecurity team removes the compromised service account from the directory group. Which of the following should the cybersecurity team do next to prevent repeat instances of this issue?

options.A: Enable two-factor authentication on the virtual network console.
options.B: Reset the logging service account to use a long and complex password.
options.C: Disable RDP on the production virtual machines.
options.D: Create a scoped administrative role for the logging service account.

discussion.author: ef74e4b
discussion.html:
D. Create a scoped administrative role for the logging service account

The root cause of the incident is excessive privileges granted to a service account. The logging service account was given full directory administration privileges, which allowed it to add itself to the VNet Console Administrators group and delete a production VM.

discussion.author: veteran_tech
discussion.html:
Why this is the right answer

This incident happened because the logging service account had excessive privileges:

It was previously granted full directory admin rights

That allowed it to add itself to the VNet Console Administrators group

Once in that group, it could delete production resources

This is a classic violation of the Principle of Least Privilege.

The root cause is overprivileged service accounts, not weak authentication or VM access.

The correct long-term preventive control is to:

Remove broad directory admin rights

question_html: A cloud administrator is implementing backups for a virtual file server with a large number of daily changes to files. The backups have historically caused performance issues on the server. As a result, the company has asked for backups to be completed as quickly as possible. The administrator opts for an incremental backup technology. Which of the following statements best explains the administrator's choice?

options.A: Differential backups cannot be used in conjunction with full backups
options.B: Differential backups are generally slower than incremental backups
options.C: Differential backups cannot be used for granular recovery.
options.D: Differential backups always consume more space than incremental backups

discussion.author: fc040c7
discussion.html: An incremental backup only copies the data that has changed since the last backup (whether it was full or incremental). This results in the smallest amount of data being transferred and the shortest backup window. In contrast, a differential backup copies all data that has changed since the last full backup. As the week progresses and more changes accumulate, differential backups become progressively larger and slower to complete compared to incremental one

discussion.author: fc040c7
discussion.html: Vertical Scaling (Scaling Up): This involves adding more resources (CPU, RAM, Storage) to the existing nodes rather than adding new ones. By increasing the capacity of the current two nodes, the engineer can mitigate resource exhaustion without violating the "no third node" rule. This is often achieved by upgrading the instance type or resizing the virtual machine.

discussion.author: fc040c7
discussion.html: Port mapping (also known as port forwarding) allows external network traffic to reach services running inside a container. By default, containers are isolated and use their own internal private IP addresses. Port mapping links a specific port on the host machine (the physical or virtual machine running the container) to a port on the container.
